parsed.explanation: Thin, mostly LGB-focused dossier. Structural signals are favourable: no trans-specific offence, same-sex conduct legal since 1989, marriage and partnerships since 2017 with strong public support, and a sexual-orientation anti-discrimination ban. Against this, gender identity is absent from the constitutional anti-discrimination ban, the hate-stirring offence and the sentencing aggravator, so a trans victim gets no identity-based recourse. Acceptance of trans people is not directly documented. No data exists on violence, police practice, border document handling, facility rules, ward placement, or the 2017 prisons ordinance. These are open questions, not documented exposures, so I weigh them lightly. The rating reflects a favourable structure with a recourse gap and an undocumented trans-specific record, placing it in the reduced-risk band.
